legend: Despite being best girl, Kirisu-sensei still is terrible at math. She has combined the concepts of greatest common factor and least common multiple together!

The greatest common multiple of two numbers a%%ZSMJ0%% and b%%ZSMJ1%% (gcm) is the largest number that both a%%ZSMJ2%% and b%%ZSMJ3%% can divide. Since this number is very large (in fact it's infinite), you are asked to find it mod some number c%%ZSMJ4%%. In this context, largest under mod means the maximum value of (d mod c)%%ZSMJ5%% over any d%%ZSMJ6%% that both a%%ZSMJ7%% and b%%ZSMJ8%% divide d%%ZSMJ9%%.
output x%%ZSMJ11%% as defined above (a∣d%%ZSMJ12%% means that a%%ZSMJ13%% divides d%%ZSMJ14%%).
input: The first line contains one integer T%%ZSMJ15%%, the number of testcases (1≤T≤3366)%%ZSMJ16%%.

The following T%%ZSMJ17%% lines each contain three integers a,b,c%%ZSMJ18%%, where a%%ZSMJ19%% and b%%ZSMJ20%% are the two numbers to find the gcm of and c%%ZSMJ21%% is the mod (1≤a,b<c≤109)%%ZSMJ22%%.
output: For each testcase, output gcm(a,b)modc%%ZSMJ23%% or maxa∣d,b∣d(d mod c)%%ZSMJ24%%.
note: If we pick d=18%%ZSMJ25%% on the first sample, we would output x=18 mod 10%%ZSMJ26%%. It is impossible to have a better answer. Note that d=48%%ZSMJ27%% or d=888888%%ZSMJ28%% also give a maximal x=8%%ZSMJ29%%.
In the second sample, picking d=189%%ZSMJ30%% gives a maximal x=9%%ZSMJ31%%.
The two auspicious 6%%ZSMJ32%%-digit numbers are codeforces gym IDs to remind us to upsolve some of our previous contests <3.
